subject: Re: Audit logs / data access evidence — next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Mills <laura.mills@fincosec.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Audit logs / data access evidence — follow up from today's call

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the deep dive. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Ask you raised: ability to produce per-user / per-API-key audit logs that show who accessed what data and when (including exports).
- Format: you prefer CSV exports with ISO timestamps + event-type and requester identity.
- Retention: you asked about configurable retention windows and our ability to provide exports for a given time range (e.g., last 6 months).
- Residency: confirmation you need logs retained in the US region only.

Next steps (Owning):
- I'll follow up with an export sample and the export schema (Rachel).
- Engineering to confirm retention/region locking and SLA for exports (Vivek).
- If that looks good, we'll provide a one-page evidence pack for procurement (Ben).

Can you confirm whether you also need a pre-signed S3 export or just a downloadable CSV from a secure console? If pre-signed S3 is required, we'll include the process and time estimate.

Thanks — aiming to get the sample to you by EOD Friday PST.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Mills <laura.mills@fincosec.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FinCo Procurement <procurement@fincobank.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Audit logs / data access evidence — follow up from today's call

Thanks Rachel — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Export format: CSV with columns for event_time (ISO8601), event_type (e.g., GENERATE, EXPORT, READ), resource_id, resource_type, requester_id, requester_role, request_ip, and action_result. Example rows would be great.

2) We need identity mapping: when requests come from our app via a system API key vs. end-user token, we need to be able to distinguish user-level access versus system-level.

3) Retention: regulatory requires 12 months immutable retention for security logs, but our procurement team may accept a project-level agreement (we can discuss retention policy options).

4) Residency: logs must be retained and exported from US-only storage for this environment.

5) Evidence: procurement would like a small bundle showing an example export, the export schema, and a short note confirming retention & residency that they can attach to the contract.

We prefer downloadable CSV from a secure portal (S3 pre-signed is acceptable but less preferred).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Laura Mills
Director, Security & Compliance | FinCo Bank
laura.mills@fincosec.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Mills <laura.mills@fincosec.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit logs / data access evidence — sample export and schema

Laura — attaching a short sample export and the schema you requested. See the attachments: 
- audit_log_sample_2026-02.csv (sample rows for the last 7 days)
- audit_log_schema.txt (field definitions and allowed values)
- redwood-audit-log-export-instructions.pdf (how to request/export from the console / API)

High-level answers: 
- Format: CSV as requested; timestamps are ISO8601 in UTC.
- User vs system: we include both requester_id and requester_type (SYSTEM_API_KEY vs END_USER). We also include an optional user_email field when available.
- Retention: by default hosted accounts have 90 days for audit logs; for Dedicated/Private we support configurable retention and can set 12 months for your environment under an addendum. We'll include wording for procurement.
- Residency: we can lock exports and storage to the US region for your dedicated environment; we'll confirm the logging pipeline components to ensure no cross-region replication (Vivek will confirm below).

Ben — can you prepare a one-page evidence note for procurement (SOC2 summary + confirmation of retention/residency) if Laura confirms the sample looks good?

Laura — if this sample matches your needs, let us know and we'll draft the evidence pack + a proposed retention clause to include in the MSA.

Thanks,
Rachel

Attachment: audit_log_sample_2026-02.csv (see attached)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Audit logs / data access evidence — technical clarifications

Quick technical notes for the thread: 

- Storage/Routing: For Dedicated/Private deployments we can enable US-only S3 buckets in the customer's account (or our US region buckets with region-locking). No logs will be cross-replicated.
- Retention: We support configurable retention policies per-tenant; enforcing immutable retention for 12 months is possible using write-once S3 + lifecycle rules. We'll document the retention configuration and handover steps.
- Exports: Exports are generated by a background job that pulls events from the audit stream and writes a CSV to a secure bucket. We'll provide either a console download link (HTTPS) or a pre-signed S3 link. Both include signed URLs and audit trail of the export action itself. Export metadata includes exporter_id and export_time.
- Identity mapping: We log both API key and downstream user identity when available. For requests proxied by FinCo, include a forwarded_user_id header so we populate the requester_id field.

I'll put together a short technical appendix to include with the evidence pack (will include example queries, retention config steps, and export job SLA). ETA Monday EOD.

Vivek
VP, Infrastructure Engineering | Redwood Inference

If you can get those artifacts over by Wednesday 04 Mar EOD EST, procurement will attach them to the SOW and we can move to contracting.

We prefer downloadable CSV via secure console (no pre-signed S3 required unless you recommend it).
